hotspots.title: Italy’s Meloni suffers major electoral reform defeat
hotspots.blurb: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government suffered a narrow defeat in a parliamentary vote on electoral reform, with her coalition failing to pass a key amendment reintroducing voter preferences. The vote exposed deep divisions within her majority, with dissenters causing the amendment to fail by a single vote.
hotspots.affect: This commands disproportionate attention due to the high-stakes political fallout, potential leadership crisis, and the intense moral and emotional framing around the defeat.

hotspots.title: Javier Milei's Central Bank reform push
hotspots.blurb: Argentine President Javier Milei is advancing a controversial reform of the Central Bank's charter, aiming to limit its ability to finance fiscal deficits and prioritize currency stability. The reform faces resistance from opposition parties and internal divisions within his coalition.
hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its high affective investment, including polarized contention, economic alarmism, and the moral framing of fiscal responsibility versus populist spending.

hotspots.title: Reform UK’s language and election material crackdown
hotspots.blurb: Reform UK proposed legislation to criminalize the use of non-English languages, including Gaelic and Scots, in election materials. The proposal has sparked widespread backlash, with critics accusing the party of promoting English supremacy and undermining linguistic diversity.
hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its moral and emotional framing, including outrage over linguistic suppression, polarized contention, and the broader implications for minority rights.

hotspots.title: Hungary’s constitutional crisis over president’s term
hotspots.blurb: Hungary's parliament, led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar's Tisza party, voted to remove President Tamás Sulyok from office through a constitutional amendment. The move has sparked a constitutional crisis, with opposition parties and international observers criticizing the government for undermining democratic norms.
hotspots.affect: This commands attention due to its high affective investment, including alarmist framing, moral panic over democratic backsliding, and polarized contention between domestic and international actors.
